featured_reviews.name: Kalpesh Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text:
*Virar*

Virar station is the northernmost terminus of the Western Railway's suburban network in Mumbai, and if you've ever stood on its platform during rush hour, you already know — this place is not for the faint-hearted.

Crowds & Capacity

This is where the station earns its reputation. Virar is one of the busiest originating stations on the entire Western line, and peak-hour crowds are genuinely intense. The mad scramble for seats when a train pulls in is practically a local sport. Expect to be pushed, jostled, and tested. If you board here early in the morning, you might get a seat — that small mercy is the silver lining.

Connectivity

For residents of Virar and surrounding areas like Nala Sopara and Vasai, this station is a lifeline. The frequency of trains, especially fast trains to Churchgate, has improved over the years. The recent addition of AC local services has been a genuine upgrade in comfort, though the fare difference keeps most daily wage commuters on the regular trains.

Infrastructure

The station has multiple platforms, foot overbridges, and basic amenities like water and food stalls. That said, the infrastructure constantly feels like it's playing catch-up with the population it serves. Cleanliness is inconsistent — some days are fine, others not so much. The area outside the station is chaotic with auto-rickshaws and vendors competing for space.

featured_reviews.name: Kshitij Srivastava
featured_reviews.review_text: Virar is a railway station on the western line of the Mumbai local train network. Virar was the northernmost station on the first regular suburban train service of the erstwhile BB&CI railway that commenced on 12 April 1867. The station was remodeled in 1913. It is a terminating station for Virar bound local trains. It is very crowded especially during peak hours.

featured_reviews.name: Uttam Nile
featured_reviews.review_text:
Virar Railway Station is an important and busy station on the Western line, especially for daily commuters. Connectivity is good, with frequent local trains towards Mumbai and nearby areas.
However, the station gets extremely crowded, particularly during peak hours, making travel hectic and uncomfortable. Cleanliness is average, and better crowd management and maintenance are needed.
The surrounding area has good availability of autos, buses, and shops, which is convenient. Overall, it’s a useful station but can improve in terms of cleanliness and handling the heavy rush.

featured_reviews.name: Mayank Masiwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the busiest railway stations on the Western Line.

It is one of the main terminating and originating stop for a lot of locals on the western line.

It serves as a major local changing point for people staying beyond Virar (Vaitarana to Dahanu).

It's almost at the centre of Churchgate & Dahanu Road.

The distance from Virar to Churchgate is 60 kms & from Virar to Dahanu Road is 64 kms.

Virar station consists of 8 platforms which performs the function as follows:

Platform No 1, 2 & 3 are the originating & terminating platform for locals running between Churchgate & Virar.

Platform No 4 serves as down main line & Platform No 5 serves as up main line.

Platform No 6 is a loop line platform specially used by the shuttles originating from Virar.

Also Platform No 4, 5 & 6 are used for originating & terminating locals for sometimes throughout the whole.

Platform No 3A & 4A are the originating & terminating platform for locals running between Dahanu Road & Virar.

Currently Virar station is undergoing a massive change and this will make Virar one of the best station with 4 new platforms addition, making Virar station a station with almost 12 platforms.

featured_reviews.name: RJ SKR
featured_reviews.review_text: This station still needs to be updated. There are narrow exits from the east and west sides of the station. If this city had been built by CIDCO, it would have seen a different picture today. Due to the long coastline to the west and the pilgrimage sites to the east, the station has not developed as much as it should from the point of view of tourism.

featured_reviews.name: sudarshan mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Being one of the busiest hubs on the Western Line, Virar Railway Station is the true lifeline for North Mumbai and Palghar. It serves as the primary gateway for anyone traveling towards Dahanu Road; almost all Dahanu-bound locals either start or terminate here, making it a critical transit point.
The station has seen massive upgrades recently with the widening of Platforms 3A and 4A to accommodate 15-coach trains, which has slightly helped with the insane peak-hour rush. While the introduction of more AC locals is a plus for comfort, it has made the regular non-AC trains even more crowded. The new Platform 5A and the ongoing work for the high-speed rail and quadrupling project show that the station is evolving. It’s always crowded, but the connectivity to both Churchgate and the Dahanu stretch is unmatched. Expect heavy crowds during morning and evening peaks

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Reliance Fresh in Virar offers a convenient shopping experience for residents of the area. Situated in a bustling locality, the store is easily accessible and well-stocked with a wide range of grocery items, fresh produce, household essentials, and personal care products. The layout is thoughtfully organized, making it easy to navigate aisles and find what you need efficiently. The staff is generally helpful and courteous, enhancing the overall shopping experience. Additionally, the store often offers attractive discounts and promotions, making it a preferred choice for budget-conscious shoppers. However, during peak hours, especially on weekends, the store can get crowded, leading to longer wait times at the checkout counters. Overall, Reliance Fresh in Virar fulfills the daily shopping needs of the community effectively, but occasional overcrowding could be addressed to further enhance customer satisfaction.
